acceptance_criteria.text: With a valid shipped scope-diff configuration, untracked enumeration excludes the configured patterns, including `.cache/**`, `tmp/**`, `libs/**/tmp/**`, and `apps/**/tmp/**`, without relying on a hardcoded exclusion array.
A missing, malformed, or empty scope-diff configuration causes measurement to fail with a hard error; it never silently proceeds with an incomplete exclusion policy.

When untracked enumeration reports a trailing-`/` nested-repository entry, scope-diff measurement completes without attempting to count that directory; an encountered symlink or other unsupported non-regular file still fails closed.

Template-export integration and in-process tests create scaffolds beneath `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR` when cargo supplies it, and remain runnable through an invocation path where the variable is not defined.
The host-first consumer scaffold tests no longer retain a `TempDir` in static process-lifetime storage, and their scaffold lifecycle permits cleanup after test use.
The test-path binary transplant uses a same-filesystem hard link and the resulting target remains byte-identical to its source.
Production template export continues to copy its binary and produces the same production export behavior and artifacts as before this track.

constraints.text: The scope-diff exclusion configuration is mandatory and fail-closed: absent, invalid, or empty configuration is a hard error rather than an implicit fallback to a partial or hardcoded policy.
The directory-entry exception is structural and non-configurable; it must not relax fail-closed behavior for symlinks or other non-regular files.
Test scaffold placement must keep retained artifacts within a cargo-cleanable or `sotp maintenance`-cleanable location instead of the shared `/tmp` area.
The hard-link optimization is limited to the test transplant path and must preserve the existing byte-identical assertion; production export continues to copy its binary.

goal.text: Eliminate the workflow failures and disk-pressure recurrence caused by untracked nested repositories and template-export test scaffolds, while preserving the production template-export contract.

in_scope.text: Replace the hardcoded scope-diff exclusion set with an operator-owned configuration under `.harness/config/`; load it for untracked-path enumeration as top-level git exclusion pathspecs. The shipped configuration includes the current exclusions plus `.cache/**`, `tmp/**`, `libs/**/tmp/**`, and `apps/**/tmp/**`.
Exclude trailing-`/` directory entries reported by `git ls-files --others` from the untracked measurement set, while retaining existing fail-closed handling for other non-regular filesystem entries.
Place template-export test scaffolds under `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR` when it is available, with a defined fallback for test invocation paths where that environment variable is absent.
Remove the process-lifetime `static OnceLock<TempDir>` sharing pattern from `consumer_scaffold_host_first.rs` so its scaffold lifecycle no longer bypasses cleanup.
Use a same-filesystem hard link for the test-path transplant of `bin/sotp`, retaining byte-identity verification for the transplanted binary.

out_of_scope.text: Changing the production template-export behavior, output artifacts, or its binary-copy transplant mechanism.
Treating periodic `/tmp` cleanup as the permanent remediation for the scaffold leak.
